courses.title: Python
courses.tagline: From your first print() to decorators and a real project
courses.blurb: Learn Python by writing it. Every lesson has examples you can edit and run in the browser, exercises that are checked by tests, and a quiz. Examples use collections and finance data, so the skills transfer straight to work.
courses.audience: Complete beginners, and Excel users who want to automate their work.
courses.needs: Nothing. Start at lesson 1 and run every example.
outcomes: Write Python programs with variables, loops, functions and classes
Read and write files, CSV and JSON
Test your code and structure a small project

modules.title: Getting started
modules.blurb: Printing, variables, numbers and text: the building blocks of every program.

modules.title: Decisions and loops
modules.blurb: Make programs choose with if, repeat with for and while, and talk to the user.

modules.title: Collections
modules.blurb: Lists, tuples, sets and dictionaries: storing many values and finding things fast.

modules.title: Functions
modules.blurb: Package code into reusable functions, pass data in and out, and handle errors.

modules.title: Organising code
modules.blurb: The standard library, files, CSV and JSON, and your own classes.

modules.title: Advanced Python
modules.blurb: Inheritance, dataclasses, generators, decorators, type hints and testing, then a project.

courses.title: Data Analysis with pandas
courses.tagline: The library most Python data work runs on, practised on collections data
courses.blurb: NumPy foundations, then the pandas skills analyst roles ask for most: reading and exploring, selecting, cleaning, groupby, pivot tables, merges and time series, ending in a monthly portfolio report. Best after Python modules 1–4. Loads pandas (about 8 MB) the first time.
courses.audience: Analysts who work in Excel and want to do the same work faster and repeatably in Python.
courses.needs: Python modules 1–4 (variables to functions). Excel experience helps.
outcomes: Load, clean and explore real data files
Filter, group, pivot and join tables
Build a monthly portfolio report with one function

modules.title: Start here
modules.blurb: Everything you already do in Excel, translated into pandas.

modules.title: NumPy foundations
modules.blurb: Fast maths on whole arrays at once: the engine underneath pandas.

modules.title: DataFrames
modules.blurb: Series and DataFrames, reading a CSV, and getting to know a dataset.

modules.title: Selecting and sorting
modules.blurb: Columns, rows, filters, loc and iloc, sorting and ranking.

modules.title: Cleaning data
modules.blurb: Missing values, wrong types, messy text and duplicates.

modules.title: Transform, group and reshape
modules.blurb: New columns, buckets, groupby, pivot tables and crosstabs.

modules.title: Combining data and time
modules.blurb: Joining tables like SQL, and working with dates and monthly trends.

modules.title: Project
modules.blurb: A full portfolio report from raw files, the way it is done at work.

courses.title: SQL with Python
courses.tagline: The skill analyst job postings ask for most, on a real database
courses.blurb: Write real SQL against a SQLite database of collections data: SELECT and GROUP BY, JOINs, safe parameters and transactions, CTEs and window functions, then hand results to pandas. Best after Python modules 1–4.
courses.audience: Anyone who needs data from a database, the most-requested skill in analyst roles.
courses.needs: Python lessons 1–6 help but are not required for the SQL itself.
outcomes: Write SELECT, GROUP BY and JOIN queries
Change data safely with parameters and transactions
Use window functions and move results into pandas

modules.title: Querying
modules.blurb: What a database is, then SELECT, filters, sorting, aggregates and GROUP BY.

modules.title: Joining and changing data
modules.blurb: JOINs, safe parameters, inserts, updates and transactions.

modules.title: Advanced SQL with pandas
modules.blurb: CTEs, window functions and moving results into pandas.

courses.title: Charts with Matplotlib
courses.tagline: Turn analysis into charts that make a point
courses.blurb: Python's standard charting library: figures and axes, choosing the right chart, rupee and percentage axes, plotting from pandas, multi-chart dashboards and report-ready visuals. Best after the first pandas modules. Loads Matplotlib (about 9 MB) the first time.
courses.audience: Anyone who presents numbers in reports or slides.
courses.needs: Python basics; the later lessons use a little pandas.
outcomes: Draw line, bar, histogram and scatter charts
Format axes in ₹ and %
Design report charts that make one clear point

modules.title: Charts for reports

courses.title: React
courses.tagline: Build interactive web interfaces, live in your browser
courses.blurb: The library behind this portfolio. Write components, props, state, lists, forms and effects with a live preview that updates as you type, and exercises checked by clicking and typing in what you build. Uses React 19.

courses.needs: Nothing required. A little HTML helps; JavaScript is explained as you go.
outcomes: Write components with props and state
Build lists, forms and live filters
Load data with effects and build a small dashboard

modules.title: Making it interactive

modules.title: Real apps
modules.blurb: Effects and loading data, then a complete mini dashboard.

courses.title: Kubernetes
courses.tagline: Run apps in containers that scale, heal and update themselves
courses.blurb: Containers and pods, Deployments that heal themselves, Services, configuration and resources, zero-downtime rollouts and rollbacks. Practise real kubectl commands and YAML on a simulated 3-node cluster you can watch.

Write Deployment, Service and ConfigMap YAML
Scale, update and roll back an app with kubectl

site.intro: Web development from "how does a web page reach my screen?" to security, rendering strategies and architecture. Runnable examples show a live page you can edit; others come from real projects like shops, blogs, portfolios and dashboards.

python.intro: Everything you need to know about Python, from your first print() to how professionals write fast, tested, production code. Every example runs in your browser.

pandas.intro: pandas from the first table to production-grade pipelines. Examples use movies, shops, weather, sport and stock prices, and every one runs in your browser.

sql.intro: SQL from your first SELECT to query plans, data modelling and warehouses. Examples use books, schools, shops and flights, and every runnable one uses a real SQLite database in your browser.

viz.intro: Data visualisation from your first line chart to honest, publication-quality graphics. Examples cover weather, sport, health, music and markets, and every chart is drawn in your browser.

react.intro: React from your first component to concurrent rendering and Server Components. Examples cover to-do lists, shops, quizzes, weather and chat, and the runnable ones show a live preview as you type.

jira.intro: Jira from your first work item to running many teams at scale. Examples come from software, marketing, HR, events and IT support, because Jira is used far beyond engineering.

k8s.intro: Kubernetes from "what is a container?" to security, scheduling and GitOps. Examples cover web shops, APIs, databases, batch jobs and streaming. Where you see a practice cluster, type real kubectl commands.
